title: How to work with Claims in ASP.NET Core Identity
description: Use claims to represent fine-grained user properties and permissions.

data.text: A **claim** is a name-value pair that represents a single fact about a user — for example, their department, seniority level, or access region. Unlike roles (which are broad categories), claims let you express precise, granular permissions.

terms.definition: A name-value pair (e.g. Department = Engineering) that describes a user attribute.
A collection of claims plus an authentication type. One ClaimsPrincipal can contain multiple ClaimsIdentity objects.
The object that represents the authenticated user. Accessible via HttpContext.User.
Adds a new claim to a user in the AspNetUserClaims table.
Removes a specific claim from a user.

cards.title: Roles
cards.description: Broad, named groups (e.g. Admin, Manager). A user belongs to zero or more roles.

data.text: HttpContext.User is a ClaimsPrincipal that contains all the current user's claims. Pass it to a view to render them in a table.

data.title: ClaimsController.cs — list current user's claims
Index.cshtml — claims table
Note
data.text: A role is just a special type of claim. When you see a claim with type ClaimTypes.Role, that represents the user's role membership.
Inject UserManager<AppUser> into ClaimsController. The Create POST action builds a Claim object and calls AddClaimAsync. The Delete action finds the claim and calls RemoveClaimAsync.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Claims Manager
data.description: Create a UI to view, add, and remove claims for the currently logged-in user.
steps: Create ClaimsController with Index (GET), Create (GET+POST), and Delete (POST) actions.
Create Index.cshtml with a table of current claims and a Delete button per row.
Create Create.cshtml with inputs for Claim Type and Claim Value.
Use UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User) to get the current user.
Log out and back in after adding a claim to see it in the table.
data.expectedOutcome: You can add a new claim (e.g. Department, Engineering), see it in the claims table, and delete it. Changes take effect after re-login.

items.hint: Use GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User) to get the current user.

items.text: AddClaimAsync creates a Claim and stores it in AspNetUserClaims
RemoveClaimAsync removes a specific claim by matching Type, Value, and Issuer
Claims table renders User.Claims ordered by Type

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Claims are name-value pairs representing user attributes.
HttpContext.User is a ClaimsPrincipal containing all current claims.
UserManager.AddClaimAsync / RemoveClaimAsync manage claims in the database.
Claims are loaded from AspNetUserClaims when the user signs in.
data.takeaway: Claims give you fine-grained control over what each user can do. Next, combine roles and claims into reusable authorization policies.
